item.title: Our guide to the best long-term yacht charter destinations
item.description: It can be difficult making the final choice from the many long-term yacht charter destinations available. We don’t make it any easier by offering the most choice with over 50 amazing destinations and prime cruising grounds to sail! Your first hurdle is crew consensus. You might want the Caribbean and someone else wants the Pacific. You could be dreaming of getting away from everyone and everything and your crew have declared they want to get to know the locals really well. When it comes to long-term yacht charters, the first thing you need to consider is the criteria that will make it a success for you and your crew. Be prepared to compromise! Narrow down everyone’s interests Are you working remotely onboard and sailing in your free time? If you are, you might want long-term yacht charter destinations that are quiet in the day – a busy marina may not suit. You might want to make sure your marina is away from the nightlife if a good night’s sleep is important to you. Find out why long-term yacht charters are the perfect choice for those wanting to work remotely somewhere a little different. Then again, you might thrive in the heart of a busy social life! If you like to relax after work eating out and chatting at a bar, then you might want to make sure you don’t have to travel far from your yacht. Choosing a marina near a lively town might become crucial to you. Think about if you want to get closer to nature, learn new water sports, absorb new culture or take in amazing scenery. Or maybe the stability of the Wi-Fi is the number one priority? Start with writing a list of the things you want to be able to do at your chosen destination and then match them to your destination shortlist. One thing to keep in mind is, does your destination require a certain level of experience? Check out our guide to whether you are qualified . Long-term yacht charter destinations for working remotely Great destinations that have interesting cruising grounds you can enjoy after work or for longer sails at the weekend include: British Virgin Islands US Virgin Islands Bahamas, Exumas Greece Croatia Tahiti If you want a sailing adventure, read our suggested itineraries for the Mediterranean and South Pacific, two key long-term charter destinations. Mediterranean long-term yacht charters Immerse yourself in the architecture and culture of ancient civilizations, island hopping and some of the world’s most fantastic sailing grounds and marinas. Benefit from great infrastructure and short passages. When is the best time to sail sabbatical in the Mediterranean? The best time to sail a Mediterranean sabbatical charter is between April and September, with the southern and eastern parts enjoying warmer conditions all year. Keep in mind that August is the peak month for visitors and it can be very crowded, especially in the northern Mediterranean. Avoid the northern Mediterranean between October to March due to low temperatures and potentially strong winds. The Aegean Sea is exposed to the northerly meltemi between July and August and it can get very windy. Mediterranean long-term yacht charter itinerary: eight months If you love nature, sail an eight-month Mediterranean sabbatical from Crete to Sicily: Crete pick up Crete to Rhodes (100nm) Rhodes Turkey’s coast Aegean Islands Piraeus, Athens Athens to Ionian Islands Ionian Islands/Albania/Montenegro. Passage to Catania, Sicily (250nm) Messina Strait & Aeolian Islands Passage to Naples (150nm) Naples/Rome. Passage to northern Sardinia (140nm) Sardinia/Corsica. Passage to Mallorca (270nm) Mallorca/Ibiza. Passage to Spain/Cartagena (200nm) Southern Spain. Passage to Cagliari/Sardinia (220nm) Cagliari/Sardinia. Passage to Southern Sicily (200nm) Southern Sicily Sicily drop off. South Pacific long-term yacht charters Explore the world’s largest lagoon in New Caledonia for amazing marine life, or sail over to charming Vanuatu to explore remote island villages and active volcanoes. item.title: NEW! Electric concept cruiser available for BVI charters
item.description: A new way of boating The Beneteau brand’s boat building legacy dates back to 1884 when Benjamin Beneteau founded the BENETEAU boatyard in France, later producing the region’s first engine-powered fishing boat in 1909. Today, Beneteau yachts remain one of the largest and most respected brands in the industry with continued innovations in terms of both boats of processes. It’s no surprise that they continue to challenge boundaries with a new reimagined hybrid electric “monohull”. A modern alternative to charter monohull & catamaran sailing Their latest venture follows extensive research dedicated to listening to the voices of countless charter guests, and collecting invaluable data about their real-world experiences. The result is the exciting new electric Island Cruising Concept designed specifically for idyllic charter holidays on the water. Step aboard this new concept boat and experience cruising at a peaceful pace, similar to a sailboat, but without the hassle of sail handling. Enjoy freedom and autonomy with hybrid electric technology, along with spacious living areas similar to a catamaran and comfortable accommodations for up to 8 guests. Sustainability meets cruising pleasure With an eye toward eco-conscious cruising combined with superior onboard comfort, Beneteau has engineered the Island Cruising Concept to operate for extended periods under full electric, emissions-free power – the ultimate choice for eco-conscious boating enthusiasts. Around 30 to 50% of the boat’s energy requirement is achieved through the power of the sun, with large roof-mounted solar panels. Charterers can enjoy easy cruising from one island to the next with a full electric range of more than 2.5 hours at 7kts. The boat’s software system ensures stress-free energy management. And, of course, a propulsion back-up is provided with the generator providing a range of nearly 250NM at 7kts. Take your charter vacation to the next level with a boat that’s respectful to the environment, and also more enjoyable with the complete absence of noise – just peaceful, silent operation – similar to sailing but with less effort! You can even make your vacation budget go further with exceptional savings through fuel efficiency. It’s also worth noting that this boat recently won an award as the Eco-Focused Launch of the Year (Over 10m LOA category), at the IBI METS Trade/Boatbuilder Awards 2024 . Indoor & outdoor living spaces blend seamlessly The main living space aboard the Island Cruising Concept is covered for protection from the elements, while providing an open-air experience that’s wide open on all sides for fresh breezes, expansive views and an unparalleled feeling of oneness with nature and the sea. This covered living space is light and bright, with 360 views and houses an outdoor kitchen, dining table, and bench lounging seat, as well as a comfortable helm station. Platforms at the back and foldout terraces on either side further expand the space and open feel, while providing easy access to the water for swimming and water sports. Doorways on either side of the covered living area allow easy access to the lounging areas on the bow. Here, guests can sunbathe or take in the stars at night from the comfortable padded bench seating and sunbed lounge areas that rival the space on the bow of a catamaran. When ready to retire for the evening, tuck below to discover four comfortable guest cabins with ensuite baths, plus a single forepeak crew cabin. Superior design for ultimate chartering comfort Comfort and efficiency aboard the Island Cruising Concept is further enhanced through a new hull shape called mono-maran, featuring a monohull shape in the bow area that widens to mimic a catamaran shape toward the back. The result is a shape that helps boost fuel efficiency under power. Most importantly, stability and comfort are greatly improved whether underway or at anchor.
